                self.pos = end_pos + 2

        return self.source[self.pos : self.pos + length]

    def consume(self, expected):

            return True
        return False

                elif esc == 'f': res += '\f'; self.pos += 1
                elif esc == '0': res += '\0'; self.pos += 1

                elif esc == '"': res += '"'; self.pos += 1

            'digit': r'\d',
            'word': r'\w',

            'tab': r'\t',
            'return': r'\r',
            'vertical': r'\v',
            'feed': r'\f',
            'boundary': r'\b',
            'start': '^',
            'end': '$',

            self.expect('of')
            expr = self.parse_expression(in_quantifier=True)
            self.skip_whitespace()
            if not expr.endswith('}') and not expr.endswith(')'): # This is a bit weak

                # If it was capture { ... }, it ends with )
                # If it was a symbol, it doesn't.

                 pass

            self.expect(';')
            return self.variables[name]

        expr = self.parse_expression()
        needs_semi = True
        if expr.startswith('(?') or expr.startswith('('):

            needs_semi = False
        
        if needs_semi:
            self.expect(';')
        return expr

    def parse_quantifier(self):
        self.skip_whitespace()
        if self.consume('some'): return '+'
        if self.consume('any'): return '*'
        if self.consume('option'): return '?'
        
        start = self.pos
        while self.pos < len(self.source) and self.source[self.pos].isdigit():
            self.pos += 1
        if self.pos > start:
            num1 = self.source[start:self.pos]
            self.skip_whitespace()
            if self.consume('to'):
                self.skip_whitespace()
                start2 = self.pos
                while self.pos < len(self.source) and self.source[self.pos].isdigit():
                    self.pos += 1
                if self.pos > start2:
                    num2 = self.source[start2:self.pos]
                    return f"{{{num1},{num2}}}"
                else:
                    self.error("expected amount")
            return f"{{{num1}}}"
        return None

    def parse_statements(self):
        res = ""
        while self.pos < len(self.source):
            self.skip_whitespace()
            if self.pos >= len(self.source) or self.peek() == '}':
                break
            res += self.parse_statement()
        return res
